questions.question: If 14 # 13 = 9 and 27 # 36 = 18, then 46 # 31 = ?
questions.solution:
Here, the digits of the number are added in itself and # means “+” i.e.

14 # 13 = 9 → (1 + 4) + (1 + 3) = 5 + 4 = 9.

27 # 36 = 18 → (2 + 7) + (3 + 6) = 9 + 9 = 18.

Similarly,

46 # 31 = ? → (4 + 6) + (3 + 1) = 10 + 4 = 14.

Thus, 14 is the correct alternative.

questions.question:
Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct?

72 - 12 + 8 × 6 ÷ 24 = 30
questions.solution:
Here, we use the BODMAS table given below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f17fe402f98bb01e6c434026861e42229a2db5fdddb9ac339c012f7a2b73afa8.png] 

Given:

⇒ 72 - 12 + 8 × 6 ÷ 24 = 30

(1) - and ÷

⇒ 72 - 12 + 8 × 6 ÷ 24 = 30

After changing the signs:

⇒ __**72 ÷ 12**__ + 8 × 6 - 24 = 30

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 6 + __**8 × 6**__ - 24

⇒ 6 + 48 - 24

⇒ 54 - 24 = 30

⇒** '72 ÷ 12 + 8 × 6 - 24 = 30'**

Here, the equation is **satisfied.**

(2) - and +

⇒ 72 - 12 + 8 × 6 ÷ 24 = 30

After changing the signs:

⇒ 72 + 12 - 8 × __**6 ÷ 24**__ = 30

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 72 + 12 - __**8 × 0.25**__

⇒ 72 + 12 - 2

⇒ 84 - 12 = 72

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

(3) - and ×

⇒ 72 - 12 + 8 × 6 ÷ 24 = 30

After changing the signs:

⇒ 72 × 12 + 8 - __**6 ÷ 24**__ = 30

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ __**72 ×**____** 12**__ + 8 - 0.25

⇒ 864 + 8 - 0.25

⇒ 872 - 0.25 = 871.75

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

(4) × and ÷

⇒ 72 - 12 + 8 × 6 ÷ 24 = 30

After changing the signs:

⇒ 72 - 12 + __**8 ÷ 6**__ × 24

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 72 - 12 + __**1.33 × 24**__

⇒ 72 - 12 + 32

⇒ 104 - 12 = 92

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

Hence, the correct answer is "**- and ÷**".

questions.question: The procedure to remove waste products and excess fluid from the blood when the kidneys stop working properly is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dialysis**__.

 
• The procedure to remove waste products and excess fluid from the blood when the kidneys stop working properly is called dialysis.
 
 
• The dialysis method is useful for the person whose kidneys can no longer perform these functions naturally.
 
• The first successful dialysis was performed in 1943.
 
• The first dialysis system was developed by Leonard Rowntree and John Abel in 1913.
 
• Dialysis works on the principles of the diffusion of solutes and the ultrafiltration of fluid across a semi-permeable membrane.
 
• Hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis are the two main types of dialysis.
 
 
 
• The blood is **filtered** by nephrons, the functional units of the kidney.
 
• This blood is** purified** by the kidneys and circulated onto the rest of the body.

Types of Dialysis:

 
• Hemodialysis - 

 
 
• This process uses an artificial kidney to remove waste and extra fluid from the blood.
 
• The blood is removed from the body and filtered through the artificial kidney.
 
• The filtered blood is then returned to the body with the help of a dialysis machine.
 
 
 
• Peritoneal dialysis:
 
 
• Peritoneal dialysis involves surgery to implant a peritoneal dialysis (PD) catheter into your abdomen.
 
• The catheter helps filter your blood through the peritoneum, a membrane in your abdomen.
 
• During treatment, a special fluid called dialysate flows into the peritoneum.
 
• The dialysate absorbs waste.
 
• Once the dialysate draws waste out of the bloodstream, it’s drained from your abdomen.
 
• This process takes a few hours and needs to be repeated four to six times per day.

questions.question: The rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends money to commercial banks is called as _______.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Repo Rate is the interest rate at which the R**eserve Bank of India (RBI) lends money to commercial banks.**
 
• It is a crucial tool used by the RBI to regulate liquidity in the banking system.
 
• When the RBI wants to infuse liquidity,** it reduces the repo rate**, making borrowing cheaper for banks.
 
• Conversely, when the RBI wants to tighten liquidity, **it increases the repo rate,** making borrowing more expensive for banks.
 
• The repo rate influences other interest rates in the economy, including lending rates for consumers and businesses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** ​Reverse Repo Rate**__

 __
 
• **​**__The Reverse Repo Rate is the interest rate at which **commercial banks lend money to the RBI.**
 
• It is the **opposite of the repo rate**.
 
• When banks have excess funds, they can deposit them with the RBI at the reverse repo rate.
 
• The reverse repo rate helps the RBI manage liquidity by absorbing excess funds from the banking system.
 
 
 
• __**CRR**__ 
 __
 
• The **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** is the percentage of total deposits that banks are required to keep with the RBI in the form of cash reserves.
 
• It is a **tool to control the money supply in the economy.**
 
• By adjusting the CRR, the RBI can influence the amount of money available for lending by banks.
 
• A higher CRR means banks have less money to lend, while a lower CRR increases their lending capacity.
 
 
 
• **SLR**__
 __
 
• **​**__The **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** is the percentage of total deposits that banks must maintain in the form of liquid assets (such as **government securities, gold, and cash**).
 
• It ensures that banks have a certain level of liquidity to meet their obligations.
 
• The SLR is set by the RBI and serves as a safety net for banks.
 
• Unlike the CRR, which is in the form of cash, the SLR allows banks to hold liquid assets other than cash.

questions.question: The area of a sector of a circle with central angle 60° is A. The circumference of the circle is C. Then A is equal to:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The total area of a circle in terms of circumference C is given directly by Aₜₒₜₐₗ = C² / 4π.

A sector with a central angle of 60° covers exactly 60° ÷ 360° = 1/6 of the total area of the circle.

Area of sector (A) = (1/6) × (C² / 4π) = C² / 24π.

**∴ The correct answer is C² / 24π.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Central angle of the sector (θ) = 60°

⇒ Circumference of the circle = C

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Circumference of a circle, C = 2πr (where r is the radius)

⇒ Area of a sector, A = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

**Calculations:**

⇒ From the circumference formula, we find the radius in terms of C:

⇒ r = C / 2π

⇒ Substitute the values of r and θ into the area formula:

⇒ A = (60° ÷ 360°) × π × (C / 2π)²

⇒ A = (1 / 6) × π × (C² / 4π²)

⇒ The π in the numerator cancels out with one π in the denominator:

⇒ A = (1 / 6) × (C² / 4π)

⇒ A = C² / 24π

**∴ The correct answer is C² / 24π.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: 12 men complete a work in 9 days. After they have worked for 6 days, 6 more men join them. How many days will they take to complete the remaining work?

Remaining days of work for the initial 12 men = 9 − 6 = 3 days.

Remaining work in terms of man-days = 12 men × 3 days = 36 man-days.

New number of men working = 12 + 6 = 18 men.

Days required to complete the remaining work = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Total Work = Number of Men × Days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of 1 man be 1 unit/day.

⇒ Total work to be done = 108 units

⇒ Remaining work = 108 − 72 = 36 units

questions.question: The whole surface area of a pyramid whose base is a regular polygon is 260 cm2 and the area of its base is 120 cm2. The area of each lateral face is 20 cm2. Then the number of lateral faces is:

⇒ Total Lateral Area = 260 − 120 = 140 cm²

⇒ Number of faces = 140 ÷ 20 = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

Total surface area of the pyramid = 260 cm²

Area of its base = 120 cm²

Area of each lateral face = 20 cm²

Total Surface Area = Base Area + (Number of lateral faces × Area of each lateral face)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a486dd2fb362a2d3e972bbbe9c73ad39e3d7124dd52eeea60916910f1f7b0085.png] 

**Calculations:**

The volume of a pyramid is one-third of the product of its base area and perpendicular height. Formula: V = (1 ÷ 3) × Base Area × Height.

Euler's Formula for Polyhedra

For any convex polyhedron, the number of faces (F), vertices (V), and edges (E) are related by the formula: F + V − E = 2.

questions.question: Ramesh purchases 75 articles for ₹ 10800 and sells them at a loss equal to the selling price of 5 articles. What will be the selling price of one article?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss = CP of 75 articles − SP of 75 articles = SP of 5 articles

⇒ CP of 75 articles = SP of (75 + 5) articles = SP of 80 articles

⇒ SP of 80 articles = Total CP = ₹10800

⇒ SP of 1 article = 10800 ÷ 80 = 135

**∴ The correct answer is ₹135.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total articles purchased = 75

Total Cost Price (CP) = ₹10800

Loss incurred = Selling Price (SP) of 5 articles

**Formula Used:**

Loss = Total CP − Total SP

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP of 75 articles − Total SP of 75 articles = Loss

⇒ ₹10800 − SP of 75 articles = SP of 5 articles

⇒ ₹10800 = SP of 75 articles + SP of 5 articles

⇒ ₹10800 = SP of 80 articles

⇒ SP of 1 article = 10800 ÷ 80

⇒ SP of 1 article = 135

**∴ The correct answer is ₹135.**

Profit and Loss Equation

questions.question: A student got 20% marks and failed by 72 marks. If he scores 40% marks then he gets 8 marks more than the passing marks. Find the passing marks.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in percentage = 40% − 20% = 20%

Difference in marks = 72 (shortfall) + 8 (excess) = 80 marks

Since 20% of maximum marks = 80 marks

Passing marks = 20% marks + 72 marks = 80 + 72 = 152

**∴ The correct answer is 152 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marks scored in case 1 = 20% (Failed by 72 marks)

Marks scored in case 2 = 40% (8 marks more than passing marks)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0325cf04d15cb9a0bcd2425e8bff93c596a76d62ae0e53dddf2563db14f14f26.png] 

**Calculation:**

Let the total maximum marks be x.

⇒ Passing marks = 20% of x + 72

⇒ Passing marks = 40% of x − 8

Equating both the expressions:

⇒ 20% of x + 72 = 40% of x − 8

⇒ 40% of x − 20% of x = 72 + 8

⇒ 20% of x = 80

⇒ x = (80 × 100) ÷ 20

⇒ x = 400

⇒ Passing marks = 20% of 400 + 72

⇒ Passing marks = 80 + 72 = 152

**∴ The correct answer is 152 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Passing Marks Concept

When a student fails by a certain margin, Passing Marks = Obtained Marks + Shortfall Marks.

Excess Marks Concept

When a student scores above passing marks, Passing Marks = Obtained Marks − Excess Marks.

Difference Rule

The percentage difference between the two scenarios will always be equal to the sum of the shortfall marks and the excess marks.

questions.question: Rahul has a bag which contains Rs. 1, 50 paisa, and 25 paisa coins and the ratio of number of coins is 1 ∶ 1/2 ∶ 1/3. If Rahul has a total amount of Rs 1120, then find the total value of 25 paisa coins.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of number of coins (Rs 1 : 50p : 25p) = 1 : 1/2 : 1/3 = 6 : 3 : 2

Ratio of their values = (6 × 1) : (3 × 1/2) : (2 × 1/4) = 6 : 1.5 : 0.5 = 12 : 3 : 1

Total value = 12 + 3 + 1 = 16 units

16 units = Rs 1120 ⇒ 1 unit = 1120 ÷ 16 = Rs 70

Value of 25 paisa coins = 1 unit = Rs 70

**∴ The correct answer is Rs 70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Types of coins: Rs 1, 50 paisa (Rs 1/2), and 25 paisa (Rs 1/4).

Ratio of the number of coins = 1 : 1/2 : 1/3

Total amount in the bag = Rs 1120

**Formula Used:**

Total Value = Number of coins × Denomination Value

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8addae167626ca48b4d3214795f175e45470ee09403b0f7a301a1b18e9cdb726.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Multiply the given coin ratio by the LCM of denominators (6) to convert to integers.

⇒ Number of coins ratio = (1 × 6) : (1/2 × 6) : (1/3 × 6) = 6 : 3 : 2

⇒ Let the number of Rs 1, 50 paisa, and 25 paisa coins be 6x, 3x, and 2x respectively.

⇒ Value of Rs 1 coins = 6x × 1 = 6x

⇒ Value of 50 paisa coins = 3x × 0.5 = 1.5x

⇒ Value of 25 paisa coins = 2x × 0.25 = 0.5x

⇒ Total value = 6x + 1.5x + 0.5x = 8x

⇒ According to the given data, total amount is Rs 1120.

⇒ 8x = 1120

⇒ x = 1120 ÷ 8 = 140

⇒ Total value of 25 paisa coins = 0.5x = 0.5 × 140 = 70

**∴ The correct answer is Rs 70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Coins vs Value

When the ratio of the number of coins is given, multiply it by the respective denomination to find the ratio of their values. Conversely, divide the value ratio by the denomination to find the number of coins ratio.

Common Denominations

It is a standard rule to convert all coins into rupees: 50 paisa = Rs 1/2, 25 paisa = Rs 1/4, 20 paisa = Rs 1/5, and 10 paisa = Rs 1/10.

Consistency of Units

Always ensure that both individual denominations and the total final amount are measured in the same unit (either entirely in Rupees or entirely in paise) to avoid calculation errors.

questions.question: A thief was spotted by a policeman from a distance of 225 metres. When the policeman started the chase, the thief also started running. If the speed of the thief was 11 km/h and that of the policeman was 13 km/h, how far would the thief have run, before the policeman caught up with him ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the time taken by both moving objects is constant, the ratio of the distance covered is equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Speed ratio (Thief : Policeman) = 11 : 13

Distance ratio (Thief : Policeman) = 11 : 13

Difference in distance covered = 13 parts − 11 parts = 2 parts

Given the initial distance difference is 225 m ⇒ 2 parts = 225 m ⇒ 1 part = 112.5 m

Distance run by the thief = 11 parts = 11 × 112.5 = 1237.5 metres

**∴ The correct answer is 1237.5 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance between policeman and thief = 225 m

Speed of thief = 11 km/h

Speed of policeman = 13 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66be807f0a7af36f7022e9bb9487558704e54a09eed7b85ee25b428d01b045a1.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed (same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 13 − 11 = 2 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 2 × (5/18) = 5/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 225 ÷ (5/9)

⇒ Time taken = 225 × (9/5) = 45 × 9 = 405 seconds

⇒ Speed of thief in m/s = 11 × (5/18) = 55/18 m/s

⇒ Distance covered by thief before getting caught = Speed of thief × Time taken

⇒ Distance = (55/18) × 405 = 55 × 22.5

⇒ Distance = 1237.5 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1237.5 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: S = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies are moving in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: S = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 17 : 45. One-third of the smaller is less than one-fifth of bigger by 15. The smaller number is?

Given, 10/3 units = 15 ⇒ 1 unit = 15 × 3 ÷ 10 = 4.5

Smaller number = 17 units = 17 × 4.5 = 76.5

**∴ The correct answer is 76.5.**

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the smaller number be 17x and the bigger number be 45x.

⇒ One-third of the smaller number = 17x / 3

⇒ One-fifth of the bigger number = 45x / 5 = 9x

⇒ According to the question, 9x − 17x / 3 = 15

⇒ (27x − 17x) / 3 = 15

⇒ 10x / 3 = 15

⇒ 10x = 45

⇒ x = 4.5

⇒ Smaller number = 17x = 17 × 4.5 = 76.5

**∴ The correct answer is 76.5.**

Compound Ratio

If two ratios are a : b and c : d, then their compound ratio is given by ac : bd.

Duplicate & Sub-duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is a² : b², and the sub-duplicate ratio is √a : √b.

Componendo and Dividendo

If a : b = c : d, then by the rule of componendo and dividendo (a + b) : (a − b) = (c + d) : (c − d).

questions.question: The ratio of the outer and the inner circumference of a circular path is 17 ∶ 15. If path is 40 metres wide, then what is the radius of the inner circle?

The ratio of circumferences of two circles is identical to the ratio of their radii.

⇒ 17x − 15x = 40

⇒ 2x = 40

⇒ x = 20

questions.question: Three piece of timber 143m, 78m and 117m long have to be divided into planks of the same length. What is the greatest possible length of each plank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the greatest possible length of equal planks, we need to find the HCF of the given lengths.

HCF is always a factor of the difference between the two closest numbers.

Difference between 117 and 78 = 117 − 78 = 39.

Factors of 39 are 1, 3, 13, and 39. Let's test the highest possible factor, 13.

All three lengths 143, 117, and 78 are perfectly divisible by 13.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Lengths of the three pieces of timber = 143 m, 78 m, and 117 m

**Formula Used:**

Greatest length of each plank = HCF of the given lengths

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4500b400afff70e81b2d36a4a3e9615ef0dab19a73892a950a269ace9fc03ae4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 143 = 11 × 13

⇒ Prime factorization of 78 = 2 × 3 × 13

⇒ Prime factorization of 117 = 3 × 3 × 13

⇒ The common prime factor with the lowest power is 13.

⇒ HCF (143, 78, 117) = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

It is the largest positive integer that divides each of the given numbers without leaving any remainder. It is also known as the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD).

Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)

It is the smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers. Commonly used to find when varying periodic events will happen together.

HCF Application in Real Life

HCF is strictly applied when we need to split multiple things into identical smaller sections, distribute quantities equally, or cut distinct materials into the maximum possible equal segments.

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two given numbers a and b, the product of their HCF and LCM is directly equal to the product of the original numbers: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a hole is drilled completely through a solid, the net Total Surface Area (TSA) is:

Net TSA = (TSA of Cube) − (2 × Base Area of Hole) + (Curved Surface Area of Hole)

Net TSA = 6a² − 2πr² + 2πrh

Net TSA = 6 × 14² − 2 × (22/7) × (3.5)² + 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 14

Net TSA = 1176 − 77 + 308 = 1407 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1407 cm².**

**Given:**

⇒ Edge of the solid cube (a) = 14 cm

⇒ Radius of the cylindrical hole (r) = 3.5 cm

⇒ Height of the cylindrical hole (h) = Edge of cube = 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Surface Area = (TSA of solid cube) − (2 × Area of circular bases of hole) + (CSA of cylindrical hole)

⇒ TSA = 6a² − 2πr² + 2πrh

**Calculations:**

⇒ TSA of cube = 6 × 14 × 14 = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm²

⇒ Area of 2 circular bases = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 3.5 = 77 cm²

⇒ CSA of cylindrical hole = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 14 = 308 cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area = 1176 − 77 + 308 = 1407 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1407 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Drilling a Hole on Surface Area

When a hole is drilled completely through a solid, the flat surface area corresponding to the base cuts is lost, but the newly created inner curved surface is exposed and must be added to the total area.

Important Formulas for a Cube

Volume = a³ | Total Surface Area = 6a² | Length of Body Diagonal = a√3.
